instructions: Independently derive the smallest sufficient semantic basis for all cases. Do not assume any supplied ontology, primitive vocabulary, or category list.

cases.requirement: A system moves from one condition to another; the resulting condition and the occurrence that led to it must both be reconstructable.
One component can technically perform an operation, but a separate rule determines whether performing it is permitted.
An operation has prerequisites, an attempt can occur, and the attempt may not establish that the intended external result occurred.
Two changes may occur concurrently and the representation must not invent an ordering that the available information does not justify.
A system receives a signal about something outside itself; the received signal must remain distinguishable from what actually happened outside the system.
A process terminates after an external interaction for which the final external result cannot be established; the representation must preserve that unresolved condition.
A governed modification occurs and later reconstruction must identify the relevant change without requiring an unbounded execution log.
An input may be received and retained while its source, validity, or permission to direct an operation remains unresolved.
An entity persists through a transformation even though its observable condition changes.
Two instances have the same present condition but their preceding circumstances differ; the representation must preserve the distinction when required by the task.
Whether information or a permission applies depends on time; older information must not silently acquire current validity.
Multiple operations can be combined without requiring a new irreducible semantic category solely because of the combination.

adversarial_cases.requirement: Equal present conditions with different preceding circumstances.
Equal received signals followed by different external results.
Concurrent independent changes with no justified total ordering.
Technical possibility differs from permitted performance.
A recorded signal can be wrong about an external event.
Process loss leaves the result of an external interaction unresolved.
Transformation changes observable condition while continuity remains relevant.
A received input is not automatically permitted to direct a change.
